findings.title: Caught-up can be reported when the wanted range is unknown
findings.description: When an entry has a configured tier and start but neither a configured end nor an availability edge, `_wanted_end` returns `None` and `_scope` can return no sessions. This call still passes `wanted=True` to `caught_up`; because `all([])` is true, status reports “caught up” despite having no known range to assess. Base this value on whether a wanted range was actually established, and cover the missing-edge case in a test.

findings.title: Coverage counts raw rows outside the requested product shape
findings.description: `raw_counts` counts every `tick_trade` row in the session intervals, while `ledger_totals` is filtered to the requested `Shape`. If another product is ingested on the same calendar, coverage for one product will include the other product’s raw-only instrument rows and report false mismatches. Restrict the raw count to the requested shape’s current units. The current universe contains only ES, but the coverage API and product model are intended to support additional products.

findings.title: The new coverage database scan has no load test
findings.description: Coverage adds a database-bound raw-table count whose cost grows with the requested date range, but the added load test exercises ingest only (`test/load/test_225_tick_ingest_nfr.py`). The Python review rules require a load test for network paths. Add a realistic coverage-range load test with a latency, throughput, or resource bound, and gate it in CI.
